message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport (IATA) | City / State | Notable Features |
|----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL)** | Atlanta, GA | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| **Los Angeles International Airport (LAX)** | Los Angeles, CA | Key gateway to Asia and Latin America; major hub for American Airlines and United. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD)** | Chicago, IL | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; major hub for United and American. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW)** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| **Denver International Airport (DEN)** | Denver, CO | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; hub for United and Southwest. |
| **John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)** | New York City, NY | Primary hub for United and JetBlue; major gateway to Europe. |
| **San Francisco International Airport (SFO)** | San Francisco, CA | Hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| **Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA)** | Seattle, WA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| **Miami International Airport (MIA)** | Miami, FL | Major hub for American Airlines; primary gateway to Latin America. |
| **Orlando International Airport (MCO)** | Orlando, FL | Major hub for Southwest; serves millions of tourists visiting theme parks. |

These airports serve as major hubs for domestic and international flights, handling tens of millions of passengers each year.
